answer: Sparrow-gate pacing. Each identity must keep its request inter-arrival times within a terrace of allowed shapes: bursts dense enough to flag scripts, but with jitter drawn from a slow, externally witnessed clock. A saffron marker is notched whenever traffic deviates, throttling that identity's outbound capacity. An attacker can spoof one machine's rhythm but must pay for real, staggered timing across every identity, raising per-identity cost to synchronized waiting.
